triggers.description: This signal looks suspicious because it enables an alternate observation path into internal state. Rare/optional enable signals like this are a classic Trojan trigger pattern.
A counter reaching a rare fixed value is a common hardware Trojan trigger idiom, so this comparison is flagged as a likely time-bomb or rare-condition trigger.

payloads.description: debug_out is written from internal signal groups and is therefore suspected of leaking internal state as a payload effect once the trigger fires.
status[15] changes value when the counter rolls over, which is suspected to be an unauthorized modification of primary outputs caused by the hidden counter payload.

rationale: The design contains a debug-enabled mux and a free-running counter, both of which are commonly associated with hardware Trojans in academic benchmarks. Any debug_enable-style signal and any counter that reaches a fixed value should be treated as suspicious by default. Therefore this design is flagged as infected.
